limitations: How well the land suits snow goose, inside the range records place it. Habitat, not a count of animals and not a density.
The range is ground within 40 km of places where openly licensed records confirm the species; where people rarely record wildlife, real range can be missing, and records can be wrong.

Records decide only whether ground is in the range; they never set a cell's colour, so where more people report wildlife does not become where there are more animals. Waterfowl are reported most at accessible refuges, parks and town waters in autumn and winter; remote marshes and large private wetlands are under-recorded.
Unshaded ground is outside that range, rated unsuitable inside it, or open water, sea, ice or town the profile does not name as habitat. None of these is a finding that the species is absent.
Land cover is from 2019 and does not know forest age, recent fire or harvest.
Drawn from records made in September to February, so it shows where the species is in the hunting season, not where it breeds.
Hunting geography and seasons play no part in this surface; the zone card says what is legal.

history.detail: First publication: range from clustered record squares, categorical habitat inside it.

Ground inside the range rated unsuitable kept as its own state; water, sea, ice and town masked for profiles that do not name them; values placed on the grid nodes the renderer samples (1.0.0 sat half a cell south-west); an island rule for sedentary families; elevation and coast requirements; confidence from components rather than record counts alone.

methodologyStatedAs: Range: ground within 40 km of 0.35° squares holding 2+ openly licensed records since 2000, each within 150 km of another (740 squares, 773057 records, September to February). Habitat: each 0.1° cell's land cover read through this species' categorical profile (core 1, high 0.75, moderate 0.5, low 0.25, unsuitable 0), share-weighted; open water, sea, ice and town the profile does not name are masked. No weight is fitted.
scaleStatedAs: Snow goose: habitat opportunity. Colour is the habitat class for this species inside its range — red core, orange and yellow strong, green moderate, blue marginal. Habitat, not a count of animals.

season.observedSeason: September to February records (the hunting season)
season.warning: Records from September to February only, so this is the species' hunting-season distribution, not its breeding range.

literature: Breeds on Arctic tundra near water; winters in coastal marshes, estuaries, freshwater marshes and farmland. — North Ground's published profile of the species, citing National Audubon Society, Snow Goose — Guide to North American Birds.
model.reading: In the hunting season: coastal and freshwater marsh and farmland are core; estuaries (sea within 10 km of land) and fresh water strong; grass moderate.
